clue.text: Using 6's muffler, I just make things worse

parts.note: the answer to 6 down is TASK, and a task is a job, so 6's gives the possessive job's
a comforter is a woollen scarf, a muffler

explanation.surface: Someone wrapped in a scarf confesses that their efforts only ever make matters worse.
explanation.walkthrough: '6's' points to the answer of 6 down; its synonym JOB gives the possessive. A Job's comforter, after the friends in the Book of Job, is someone whose consolation only deepens the misery.
explanation.definitionFit: A Job's comforter offers consolation that actually aggravates distress, so such a person says they only worsen things.

clue.text: Acting is jolly, I worked out, in Chauvin's style

indicators.note: worked out means solved or reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor says the jolly role was worked out to suit a character named Chauvin.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicolas Chauvin was a legendary fanatical patriot whose name gave us chauvinism, so his style is jingoistic.
explanation.definitionFit: Chauvin's name gave chauvinism, the extreme patriotism also called jingoism, so acting in his style is behaving jingoistically.

clue.text: Bar (very noisy) in Canadian resort

parts.note: to bar is to ban
ff, fortissimo, is the musical direction for very loud

explanation.surface: A very loud bar in a Canadian holiday town.
explanation.definitionFit: Banff is a resort town in Alberta's Rocky Mountains, in Canada.

clue.text: Grab a sourpuss and row badly

parts.note: to grab is to catch
taken as written
a crab is a grumpy, sour person

explanation.surface: Seize a grumpy person and row clumsily.
explanation.walkthrough: To catch a crab is a rowing term for a bad stroke where the oar blade jams in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Catching a crab is a faulty stroke in which the oar fails to leave the water, a rowing blunder.

clue.text: Deliverer wanting to exploit island

parts.note: to milk is to exploit
Man is the Isle of Man, an island between Britain and Ireland

explanation.surface: A delivery person wants to take advantage of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: A milkman delivers milk to homes, still a familiar British daily delivery round.
explanation.definitionFit: A milkman delivers milk to doorsteps, so he is a deliverer.

clue.text: Pay attention to broadcast answer

parts.note: OB is an outside broadcast
to answer a purpose is to serve it

explanation.surface: Listen carefully to the answer that is being broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe is to watch or notice carefully, to pay attention to something.

clue.text: Time to demand work

parts.note: to ask is to demand

explanation.surface: It is time to insist on some work.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a piece of work to be done.

clue.text: In the country, Roundhead, losing his head, hid in valley

indicators.note: hid in means this piece is tucked inside the other

parts.note: a ria is a long drowned river valley

indicators.note: losing his head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: the Roundheads, Parliament's side in the English Civil War, were largely Puritans

explanation.surface: In the countryside a Roundhead, beheaded, was concealed in a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing his head' fits the Civil War, but it just drops the P of PURITAN. Ruritania is the imaginary kingdom of Anthony Hope's novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruritania is the fictional Central European kingdom in The Prisoner of Zenda, a made-up country.

clue.text: Performer's singular lyrics applied to hippopotamus, perhaps

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
the lyrics of a song are its words
a hippopotamus wallows in mud, so it is an example of one that wallows

explanation.surface: A performer's solo song lyrics are written about a hippo.
explanation.definitionFit: A sword-swallower is a circus or street performer who seems to swallow a blade.

clue.text: Band's single found in the Book

indicators.note: something found in another thing sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: NT is short for the New Testament, part of the Bible, the Book
single means one

explanation.surface: A group's hit single has turned up in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a group of nine musicians, a kind of band.

clue.text: Bringing up the rear, stalks camel's killer

parts.note: to bring up the rear is to come last
straw is dried stalks of cereal plants

explanation.surface: Something at the back stalks a camel and kills it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stalks' looks like a verb of hunting, but it is the plural noun. The proverb says the last straw is what breaks the camel's back.
explanation.definitionFit: In the proverb, the final straw added to the load breaks the camel's back, so it kills the beast.

clue.text: Start boat after the others — that's not right

indicators.note: after places the boat's letters behind the ones before

parts.note: the off is the start of a race
them means the others, those people
Noah's ark is a boat

explanation.surface: A rower begins the race behind the rest and calls it unfair.
explanation.definitionFit: Off the mark means inaccurate or wide of the target, which is wrong or not right.

clue.text: Lead singers —- they are really tops

definitions.text: Lead singers —- they are really tops

parts.words: Lead singers —- they are really tops
parts.note: the leading performers in a show, or the best singers of the day, are the celebrated top names of their trade

explanation.surface: Praise for the principal vocalists, said to be the very best.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a leading performer, the top name who takes the lead role.

clue.text: Pardoning a criminal that's responsible for producing notes …

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so these letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Pardoning a lawbreaker is held to be responsible for drafting official notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' suggests memos, but it means musical notes, which a piano produces.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand piano is an instrument that produces musical notes when its keys are struck.

clue.text: Lag behind starter in dash

indicators.note: behind places the convict after the starter

parts.note: soup is a typical starter course of a meal
a lag is a convict, a con

explanation.surface: Someone lags behind the leader in a sprint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lag' and 'dash' read as racing words, but a lag is British slang for a convict and the dash is a small amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A soupcon is a tiny amount, as is a dash of something added in cooking.

clue.text: … half hidden, mischievous, but public-spirited

indicators.note: half means only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: unseen means hidden
elfish means impish, mischievous

explanation.surface: A half-concealed, naughty figure who nonetheless thinks of others.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading ellipsis joins this clue to 13 down's for surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Unselfish means putting others first, the attitude of someone public-spirited.

clue.text: Slip and slide when setting off for shopping trips

parts.note: to slip is to err, make a mistake
taken as written

indicators.note: setting off is starting out, so only the first letter of slide is used

explanation.surface: Someone slips and slides on the way to the shops.
explanation.definitionFit: Errands are short trips to get things done, such as shopping.

clue.text: Tick —- insect dropping behind in a way

indicators.note: the insect falls in behind the other pieces, so it comes last

parts.note: taken as written
St is short for street, a way
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A parasitic tick, as insects go, lags behind on a path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tick' wants to be the bloodsucking creature beside 'insect', but it is a moment, as in 'just a tick'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tick is British slang for a moment, as is an instant.

clue.text: Consort with a saint, struggling to overcome resistance

indicators.note: to overcome is to get over, so the scrambled letters go round the other one
struggling suggests flailing about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: Keeping company with a holy person who battles to beat opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consort' looks like a verb, keeping company 'with a saint', but it is the noun: the wife of a tsar.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarina was the wife of a Russian tsar, his consort.

clue.text: Composition about an adieu

parts.note: c, for circa, means about
taken as written
ta-ta is a casual goodbye, an adieu

explanation.surface: A piece of music is said to be about a farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantata is a musical composition for voices and instruments.

clue.text: In the beginning, couple embraced and made repeated noises

indicators.note: in the beginning means only the opening letter of couple is used

parts.note: to embrace is to hug

explanation.surface: At first a couple hugged and made repeated sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Chugging is the repeated dull thudding sound of an engine, so it chugged.

clue.text: Rod, not middle in age? About 40

indicators.note: about means around, so these letters go round the number
without its middle, only the first and last letters of age remain

parts.note: XL is 40 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether forty counts as not yet middle-aged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not middle in age' looks like a question about middle age, but it strips the G from AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: An axle is the rod or shaft on which a wheel turns.

clue.text: Paul chairs gathering of ancient diviners

indicators.note: gathering pulls the letters together into a new heap, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Paul presides over a meeting of soothsayers from antiquity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chairs' looks like a verb, Paul chairing a meeting, but it is anagram fodder. Haruspices were Roman diviners who read the entrails of sacrificed animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Haruspical is the adjective for haruspices, Roman soothsayers who foretold events from animal entrails.

clue.text: Start of one canal: almost the end of another

definitions.meaning: The port city at the Caribbean entrance of the Panama Canal
the large intestine, near the far end of the alimentary canal

explanation.definitionFit: Colon is the Panamanian port at one canal mouth and also the bowel near the end of the gut.

clue.text: A lot of wood to hand out

definitions.meaning: softwood timber of fir or pine, sold in planks
to distribute, as cards are given out around a table

explanation.definitionFit: Deal is fir or pine timber, and to deal is to distribute, as with cards.

clue.text: Hanging about together, lion and tiger fall out

indicators.note: to fall out is to quarrel and break apart, so these letters scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: A lion and a tiger, idling together, start to quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Loitering means lingering idly, hanging about with no purpose.

clue.text: Let out of 8

indicators.note: out of signals letters taken from inside the answer to 8 down

parts.note: the answer to 8 down is the name of the performer who downs blades

explanation.surface: A performer is let out of a show.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' refers to the answer to 8 down, SWORD-SWALLOWER, and the run of letters is taken from its second word.
explanation.definitionFit: To let something happen is to allow or permit it.

clue.text: Secret hidden at first shrub bearing seeds

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of hidden is used
a shrub bearing something carries it within, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: the oleander is an evergreen flowering shrub
corn is the seed of cereal plants

explanation.surface: A secret is concealed at the start of a shrub full of seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Hole-and-corner means furtive or clandestine, done in secret.
